title: Generic-fibre bound for dimensions in a flat family
statement: Let $S$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] with generic point $\eta$, and let $f:Y\to S$ be a flat morphism locally of finite type [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. If $r\geq0$ is an integer and $\dim Y_\eta\leq r$, then $\dim Y_s\leq r$ for every point $s\in S$, where $Y_s=Y\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-weil-residue-field] and dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Empty fibres are allowed, with dimension $-\infty$.

source.place: Tag 0H3X, lemma-relative-dimension-support-flat, with the finite type quasi-coherent module O_Y (support equal to Y).

proof.text: Fix $s\in S$ and an irreducible component $C$ of $Y_s$. By [lem-sc-scheme-sober], choose its generic point $x$. Regard $x$ as a point of $Y$ using the fibre homeomorphism of [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Since $\eta$ is generic in the integral scheme $S$, it specializes to $s=f(x)$: $\overline{\{\eta\}}=S$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-generalizations-lift] to the flat map $f$ and this specialization. It gives a point $y\in Y$ specializing to $x$ with $f(y)=\eta$, so $y$ is a point of $Y_\eta$. This argument requires neither finite presentation nor Noetherianity of $S$.

source.place: Tag 0H3X (lemma-relative-dimension-support-flat), proof with the structure sheaf; component-dimension input Tags 0GSI and 0GSJ.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover], choose an irreducible component $B$ of $Y_\eta$ containing $y$, and by [lem-sc-scheme-sober] let $z$ be its generic point. In $Y_\eta$ the point $z$ specializes to $y$; the continuous fibre inclusion and the specialization $y\leadsto x$ imply $z\leadsto x$ in $Y$. Put $Z=\overline{\{z\}}\subseteq Y$ and $Z_s=Z\cap f^{-1}(s)$ with the subspace topology. The fibre homeomorphism makes $Z_s$ a closed subset of $Y_s$ containing $x$, hence containing $C=\overline{\{x\}}$ in that fibre. The set $C$ is irreducible in $Z_s$; any irreducible subset of $Z_s$ properly containing it would be irreducible in $Y_s$, contradicting the maximality of $C$. Thus $C$ is an irreducible component of $Z_s$.

source.place: Tag 0H3X (lemma-relative-dimension-support-flat), proof with the structure sheaf; component-dimension input Tags 0GSI and 0GSJ.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-flat-fibre-component-closure-dimension] with $X=Y$, $t=\eta$, the generic point $z$ of $B$, and the component $D=C$ of $Z_s$ found in step 2. Its hypotheses are exactly the given flatness and local finite type, together with these component choices. It gives $\dim C=\dim B$. The set $B$ is closed in $Y_\eta$, so each chain of irreducible closed subsets of $B$ is also such a chain in $Y_\eta$; hence $\dim B\leq\dim Y_\eta\leq r$ by the chain definition of Krull dimension. Therefore $\dim C\leq r$. In particular no flatness of the reduced closure of $z$ has been assumed.

source.place: Tag 0H3X (lemma-relative-dimension-support-flat), proof with the structure sheaf; component-dimension input Tags 0GSI and 0GSJ.

proof.text: We have bounded every irreducible component of $Y_s$. To pass to the dimension of the whole fibre, take any finite strict chain $D_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq D_n$ of irreducible closed subsets of $Y_s$. By [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover], its largest member $D_n$ is contained in an irreducible component $C$. Each $D_i$ is closed and irreducible in $C$ with its subspace topology, and strict inclusions remain strict. Thus $n\leq\dim C\leq r$ by step 3. Taking the supremum over these chains gives $\dim Y_s\leq r$. If $Y_s$ is empty there is no such chain and its dimension is $-\infty\leq r$. Since $s$ was arbitrary this proves the conclusion. If the generic fibre is empty, step 1 shows that every fibre must be empty as well.
